newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to pause, dollar asserts influence.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to pause, dollar asserts influence.

text.p: The Brussels bourse on Thursday rose to touch the 1,900 level on the Bel-20 index for the first time but then closed lower, shrugging off Wall Street gains in the afternoon.

Investors sold some stock as the dollar fell in late trading. "Today the bourse has been more influenced by the dollar than the Dow. If the dollar strengthens again, this will be good for the export market," one dealer said.
The Bel-20 share index closed down 0.17 percent or 3.13 points to 1,891.12 after touching an intraday high of 1,900.93.

Dealers said the Bundesbank's decision to leave rates unchanged was welcomed by the market but added that investors were looking for further cuts in interest rates to encourage them to buy more stocks.
"If the Bundesbank lowers its interest rates then we might see strong bourse moves," said one dealer.
Cyclicals which had seen sharp rises in recent weeks saw losses this week as investors were awaiting more positive economic news for 1997 before buying more of its stocks.
"There is not enough positive information and confirmation that we'll see strong economic growth for 1997," a dealer said.
Oil and chemicals firm Petrofina climbed 4.14 percent to 10,700 francs as investors realised the stock was undervalued.
"Petrofina is up because people have seen that it didn't follow the stocks in the same branch last year and had lagged behind instead, now we're nearing the correct level," a dealer said.
"Petrofina will be the stock of 1997, it was a bit stuck under 10,000 francs because of OTC derivatives but they'll expire this months so we'll see further rises," another dealer said.

Utilities holding firm Tractebel fell 1.02 percent to 14,550 francs. "During the last two weeks a lot of buyers have picked up stocks in Electrabel, it looks like they've been swapping Tractebel shares for Electabel," he said.
Steel maker Cockerill fell 4.65 percent to 123 francs after news it will be replaced in the Bel-20 by electronics firm Barco on December 20.

But one dealer said it was more because of the prospect of Dutch metals group Hoogovens becoming a competitive threat to Cockerill in Belgium, following its talks with steel maker Usines Gustave Boel.
